title: Design System: A Xmas for the Ages

display.purpose: The two-line site name on the foil band.

headline.purpose: Slip titles and section titles on the red ground.

title.purpose: Sub-headings, the big spin button, game and team names.

body.purpose: All running text; ledes and hints in the soft colour.

label.purpose: Form labels, tabs, buttons, mode switch.

meta.purpose: Slip foot lines ('Slip N · kind') and voter lists.

tv-question.purpose: The question on the TV quiz stage, read across a room.

shadows.name: paper
shadows.purpose: Every slip and card: paper resting on paper.

shadows.name: paper-button
shadows.purpose: Gold buttons at rest; removed on press.

shadows.name: crown-drop
shadows.purpose: Filter on the small paper crown icon.

shadows.name: prize-crown-drop
shadows.purpose: Filter on the large crown in the prize slip.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Button lift on hover and press; off under reduced motion.

motion.name: crown-drop
motion.purpose: Crown drops onto the prize slip after a spin.

motion.name: slip-pop
motion.purpose: Prize slip arrives after a spin.

motion.name: bar-grow
motion.purpose: Vote share bars; TV scoreboard bars use .8s.

motion.name: confetti
motion.purpose: Spin landing burst; not drawn under reduced motion.

narrative.northStar: What Tumbles Out of the Cracker
narrative.overview:
The whole interface is the contents of a pulled Christmas cracker. The page itself is the cracker's red paper, striped on the diagonal; across the top runs the gold foil tube with crimped zigzag ends; everything you read or fill in is a white joke slip; every team is a tissue-paper crown in its own colour. It is loud and playful on purpose, and it stays on one theme: the red ground is the identity, so it does not flip for dark mode.

Loudness lives in the ground, the foil and the display face, never in clutter. The slips are calm, square-ish paper with a single red print rule under their title, sturdy body type and big tap targets for a middle-aged audience on phones. Hierarchy comes from weight, case and the display/body switch on a small type scale rather than from many sizes. The TV quiz screen is the same world scaled up for reading across a living room: the same crimped band, the red stage, answers on big tissue-coloured tiles.

Every gradient in the system is a hard-stop pattern (stripes, a punched hole), never a smooth blend. Depth is paper lying on paper: one short shadow, no floating cards.
keyCharacteristics: Cracker-red striped ground owns every page; single light theme by design.
Crimped gold foil band (repeating stripes, zigzag mask) as the masthead on phone and TV.
White joke slips with a 2px print-red rule under the title and a "Slip N · kind" foot line.
Six tissue-crown team colours, each with a paired text colour, carried by a drawn paper-crown icon.
Gift tags (notched end plus punched hole) for the countdown tag and the tabs.
Titan One for display, Figtree for everything you read; both self-hosted.

rules.name: The Red Ground Rule
rules.body: The striped cracker red is the page, on every surface and in every OS colour scheme. Content goes on paper laid over it; the ground is never replaced by a pale background.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: On the red ground, gold is the only colour that means "do this". Print red belongs to the paper; tissue colours belong to teams and nothing else.

rules.name: The Hard-Stop Rule
rules.body: Gradients exist only as hard-stop patterns: diagonal stripes, conic stripes, a punched-hole radial. No smooth decorative blends.

rules.name: The Weight-Not-Size Rule
rules.body: Rank comes from the display/body switch, weight (500/600/700/800) and case, on a small scale. Don't add new sizes to create emphasis.

rules.name: The Foot-Line Rule
rules.body: Slip metadata goes at the foot of the slip as a Meta line, never as a small label above the heading.

rules.name: The Short Paper Rule
rules.body: A shadow is at most a few pixels: paper resting on paper. If it reads as floating, it is wrong.

dos: **Do** keep the striped cracker red (cracker-red / cracker-red-stripe, 135deg) as the ground of every page, in light and dark OS settings alike.
**Do** put everything readable or fillable on a white joke slip with the 4px corner, the paper shadow `0 3px 3px -1px rgb(40 0 10 / .5)` and a 2px print-red rule under its title.
**Do** use foil gold for the single main action and the current selection on the red ground.
**Do** give each team its tissue colour and its paired text colour, and show it with the paper crown.
**Do** build stripes, crimps and holes from hard-stop gradients and masks (the "paper-cracker stripes" motif).
**Do** carry slip metadata in the foot line ("Slip N · kind") in Meta type.
**Do** keep tap targets at 44px or more and every motion still under reduced motion.
donts: **Don't** add a dark theme or a pale page background; the red ground does not flip.
**Don't** use soft, long or blurred elevation on slips; depth is a short paper shadow only.
**Don't** use smooth decorative gradients; stripes and holes are hard-stop.
**Don't** put a small uppercase label above a heading; slip metadata belongs in the foot line.
**Don't** use tissue team colours for anything except teams (and the TV answer tiles that borrow four of them).
**Don't** set print red on the red ground or body text in Titan One.
